brief: JPMorgan's morning briefing reports Asian equities and US/EU futures lower, USDJPY briefly below 153 hitting Japanese exporters (-3%, autos -5%), and crude extending gains ahead of Iran-Oman deal details. The desk has been neutral/tactically cautious on global equities since last Monday on four risks: terminal G4 rates, energy prices and crack spreads, politics, and the July/August forced rotation out of Tech. It still expects dips to be bought because none of those risks ends the cycle while revisions are solid, GDP is accelerating and positioning is light, so it keeps buying dips and adds cheap EU index hedges rather than cutting length. On AI, OpenAI's Astra triggered the infrastructure rerating through better cost-per-token efficiency on agentic tasks, improving adoption economics and supporting capex, but the desk argues AGI is invoked too freely and re-grossing also explains the move. BoJ risk sits in FX and rates rather than equities: half the USDJPY long unwind is done, resistance is 152. Euro-area GDP was revised from 1.8% to 2.6% annualised, driven entirely by Ireland at 47.4%.
